# Top 10 Holdings of the Nasdaq-100 Index

*Note: Data is approximate and based on my knowledge up to early 2025. Values fluctuate daily.*

| Rank | Company | Ticker | Market Cap (approx.) | P/E Ratio (approx.) | Weight (approx.) |
|------|---------|--------|---------------------|---------------------|-------------------|
| 1 | Apple | AAPL | ~$3.4T | ~33 | ~9% |
| 2 | Microsoft | MSFT | ~$3.1T | ~35 | ~8% |
| 3 | NVIDIA | NVDA | ~$3.0T | ~60 | ~7% |
| 4 | Amazon | AMZN | ~$2.3T | ~45 | ~5% |
| 5 | Broadcom | AVGO | ~$1.0T | ~175 | ~4% |
| 6 | Meta Platforms | META | ~$1.6T | ~27 | ~4% |
| 7 | Tesla | TSLA | ~$1.1T | ~170 | ~3% |
| 8 | Costco | COST | ~$420B | ~55 | ~3% |
| 9 | Alphabet (GOOGL) | GOOGL | ~$2.2T | ~24 | ~3% |
| 10 | Alphabet (GOOG) | GOOG | ~$2.2T | ~24 | ~3% |

> **⚠️ Disclaimer:** These figures are estimates based on my training data and may be outdated. For real-time data, please check sources like **Bloomberg**, **Yahoo Finance**, or **Nasdaq.com**. Rankings and weights shift frequently based on market movements.

**Key observations:**
- **Big Tech dominance** — The top 10 holdings represent roughly **50%+** of the entire index
- **AI-driven valuations** — Companies like NVIDIA and Broadcom carry elevated P/E ratios due to AI growth expectations
- **Alphabet appears twice** due to its dual share class structure (GOOGL = Class A, GOOG = Class C)
